sections.text: Revenue increased during the measured period as a result of stronger product sales and service growth. Operating performance remained supported by higher customer engagement and efficient product execution.
Operating expenses changed during the measured period as research and development spending remained elevated, while marketing and general administrative costs were managed with discipline.

A material risk was disclosed as supply-chain constraints and component availability could affect future operating results. Management highlighted the need to monitor production planning and cost discipline.
Capital expenditure increased as investments in manufacturing and product infrastructure were expanded. The company stated that spending remained aligned with long-term operational planning.
